title: Minimum Obstacle Removal to Reach Corner
summary: Given a grid with empty cells (0) and obstacles (1), determine the least number of obstacles to remove to travel from the top-left corner to the bottom-right corner.
statement: Given a grid with empty cells (0) and obstacles (1), determine the least number of obstacles to remove to travel from the top-left corner to the bottom-right corner.
constraints: Zero cells are free and one cells are removable obstacles; start and destination are zero.
Move in four cardinal directions and pay one when entering an obstacle cell.
Return the minimum number of obstacles removed along any route.
hints: This is shortest path with edge weights zero or one based on the entered cell.
A deque processes zero-cost relaxations at the front and one-cost relaxations at the back.
Relax four neighbors; appendleft for zero and append for one until no distance improves.
0-1 BFS maintains nondecreasing tentative cost like Dijkstra specialized to binary weights, so the destination distance is minimal.
editorial: 0-1 BFS maintains nondecreasing tentative cost like Dijkstra specialized to binary weights, so the destination distance is minimal.

tests.explanation: A least-cost route enters two obstacle cells before reaching the corner.
A path of zero cells reaches the destination without removing an obstacle.
